plan.summary: Build a local Web Dashboard on top of the existing `cf` CLI by first refactoring shared helpers into a reusable `src/utils.js`, then adding a dependency-free Node.js HTTP server with JSON endpoints backed only by local cache data, and finally delivering a modular dark-theme frontend that visualizes profile, rating trends, roadmap progress, tag performance, rating buckets, weakness analysis, recommendations, and submission timeline in an architecture that is easy to extend with new panels and APIs.

phases.name: Extract shared utilities
phases.description: Create `src/utils.js` and move the duplicated helper functions out of `stats.js`, `weak.js`, `next.js`, and `training.js`. Update those modules to import the shared helpers instead of maintaining local copies. Preserve existing CLI behavior and keep all current tests passing before any dashboard work starts.
acceptance: `src/utils.js` exports shared helpers including `isFiniteNumber`, `normalizeString`, `normalizeTag`, `normalizeTags`, `hasAnyCache`, `getCacheHandle`, and `formatRating`.
Duplicate implementations of those helpers are removed from `stats.js`, `weak.js`, `next.js`, and `training.js`.
Existing commands using stats, weak analysis, next recommendations, and training roadmap continue to produce the same outputs for the same cache inputs.
All pre-existing automated tests pass without modification to their expectations, except where import paths are updated internally.
tests: Add or update unit tests for `src/utils.js` covering number validation, string normalization, tag normalization, cache detection, cache handle resolution, and rating formatting.
Run the existing test suite to verify no regression in `stats`, `weak`, `next`, and `training` behavior.
Add focused regression tests that compare representative outputs before and after refactor for modules that previously owned duplicate helpers.

phases.name: Add dashboard server command
phases.description: Implement `cf serve [--port <number>]` in the CLI, using only Node.js built-in modules to start a local HTTP server. Serve a minimal dashboard HTML shell and static assets, print `Dashboard: http://localhost:<port>` on startup, return JSON content types for API routes, and shut down cleanly on Ctrl+C.
acceptance: Running `node cf.js serve` starts an HTTP server on port `3000` by default.
Running `node cf.js serve --port 3456` starts the server on port `3456`.
Startup logs exactly `Dashboard: http://localhost:<port>` with the active port.
Ctrl+C closes the server process without unhandled promise rejections or hanging sockets.
The browser root route returns the dashboard HTML shell, and unknown API routes return a JSON 404 response.
tests: Add CLI/command parsing tests for default port and explicit `--port` override.
Add integration tests that start the server, request `/`, confirm HTML is returned, and request a missing `/api/...` route to confirm JSON 404 behavior.
Add a shutdown test or harness that starts the server and verifies graceful close logic executes without throwing.

phases.name: Implement cache-backed JSON APIs
phases.description: Build the dashboard data layer and all required JSON endpoints by reading only local cache files under `~/.cf-coach/cache/`, reusing existing analysis logic where appropriate. Normalize data contracts for profile summary, rating history, tag stats, rating buckets, roadmap progress, weak analysis, next recommendations, and full submissions so the frontend can consume them consistently.
acceptance: `GET /api/profile` returns handle, rating, maxRating, rank, total accepted count, total submissions count, and total attempted problems in JSON.
`GET /api/rating-history` returns one record per contest with contest name, timestamp, and `newRating`, ordered by time.
`GET /api/tag-stats` returns per-tag accepted count, attempted count, and acceptance rate.
`GET /api/rating-buckets` returns accepted counts grouped into rating buckets matching dashboard needs, including `1600+`.
`GET /api/roadmap` returns 20 ordered phases with stage name, tag, accepted progress, target, and current-stage marker.
`GET /api/weak` returns tag gaps, rating weak zones, and roadmap gap data derived from cached submissions/problem history.
`GET /api/next` returns the current topic, stage progress, one anchor problem, and three prerequisite problems with Codeforces links.
`GET /api/submissions` returns full submission records including timestamp, rating, verdict, problem id, title, and tags.
No endpoint makes outbound Codeforces API requests; all responses are produced from local cache data only.
When cache data is missing or partial, endpoints return valid JSON errors or empty-state payloads instead of crashing.
tests: Add endpoint integration tests for each `/api/*` route using fixture cache data and assert exact response shapes.
Add unit tests for transformation logic such as attempted-problem counting, per-tag aggregation, rating bucket assignment, roadmap progress calculation, and weak-zone detection.
Add failure-path tests for missing cache, malformed cache fragments, and partial datasets to confirm stable JSON error handling.
Add a guard test ensuring the dashboard data layer does not invoke remote fetch/network code paths.

phases.name: Build dashboard shell and core panels
phases.description: Create a modular dark-theme frontend using plain HTML, CSS, and vanilla JS, organized so each dashboard panel has its own render function. Implement the profile bar, rating trend chart, roadmap panel, tag ability chart, and rating bucket chart, with fetch-based loading from the JSON APIs and responsive desktop-first layout that remains usable at 1024px width.
acceptance: The dashboard page loads without external JS/CSS libraries and fetches data from local `/api/*` endpoints.
The layout renders correctly in a desktop viewport and remains usable at `1024px` minimum width.
Profile bar shows handle, CF-colored rating, rank, total AC, total submissions, and attempted problem count.
Rating trend panel renders a line chart with non-uniform time spacing on the x-axis and rating on the y-axis.
Rating trend tooltip shows contest name and rating delta on hover.
Roadmap panel renders 20 stages with name, tag, progress, current-stage highlight, completed-state styling, and not-started styling.
Tag ability panel renders horizontal bars sorted by accepted count descending, with separate accepted and attempted bars plus acceptance-rate labels.
Rating bucket panel renders accepted-count bars for `800/900/1000/.../1600+` using Codeforces rating colors.
Frontend code is organized into reusable rendering functions/modules so adding a new panel does not require rewriting the whole page.
tests: Add frontend unit tests where practical for data formatting helpers, color mapping, bucket labeling, and sorting logic.
Add DOM/integration tests for panel render functions using mocked API payloads to verify expected text, ordering, and CSS state classes.
Add browser-level smoke tests that load the dashboard page and verify all core panels render when APIs return fixture responses.
Add visual sanity checks or screenshot-based manual test instructions for desktop and 1024px layouts.

phases.name: Add training insights panels and polish
phases.description: Complete the dashboard with the bottom training panel and submission timeline. Render weak analysis and recommendation cards with external Codeforces links, add the submission scatter plot with verdict coloring and hover details, and finish UX polish such as loading states, empty states, error display, and shared chart utilities to support future panel expansion.
acceptance: Weak analysis panel shows tags with acceptance rate below 50% and attempts at least 3, rating weak areas, and current roadmap gaps.
Recommendation panel shows current topic, stage progress, one anchor problem, and three prerequisite problems.
Clicking any recommendation card opens the Codeforces problem page in a new tab.
Submission timeline renders a scatter plot using actual submission timestamps on the x-axis and problem rating on the y-axis.
Submission points are colored by verdict: AC green, WA red, TLE orange, others gray.
Submission tooltip shows problem title, verdict, and submission time.
Dashboard shows clear loading, empty, and error states for panels when APIs are slow, empty, or unavailable.
Shared frontend utilities exist for chart scaling, tooltip handling, color mapping, and panel rendering patterns to ease future extension.
tests: Add integration tests for weak-analysis and next-problem panels using fixture responses, including external-link attributes such as `target="_blank"`.
Add rendering tests for submission timeline point placement, verdict color mapping, and tooltip content.
Add empty-state and error-state tests for every bottom-panel data source and the submissions chart.
Run an end-to-end smoke test that starts `cf serve`, loads the page, verifies all seven dashboard sections are present, and confirms data-driven interactions work on fixture cache data.
